labels.label: btzthm:BTZ_Cauchy-completness
labels.notes: Unmarked (`btzthm:BTZ_Cauchy-completness` in backticks, no ** mark), which is correct: this is a step of Step 1 of the proof (second half of BTZ_1.tex:1601), not the theorem. REPORT row is `partial`, honestly. Quote of l.1601 at docstring l.12-15 is verbatim. FAITHFULNESS against the target scope and l.1601: trace_tendsto_atTop_of_isCauchyComplete (TraceComplete.lean:596) has exactly the setting of GX.E0TraceDev.trace_tendsto_atTop (flat N, psi : E0Y -> FlatE0 N, IsOpen W, bspearY v R ⊆ W, IsE0Mor psi W, IsSpacelikeLipschitz 2 Sig, tauS continuous on {0<|z|<=R}, v + |z|/2 < tauS z, graph equivalence on bspear v R, 0 < R'' < R) with hcomp replaced by the last two fields of Causal.Flat.IsCauchyComplete (CompleteSpace (InducedLengthSpace 2 Sig), continuity of toSubtype into N); conclusion Tendsto (traceFun tauS) (comap Prod.fst (nhdsWithin 0 (Ioi 0))) atTop, i.e. tau_0 -> +infinity as r -> 0 uniformly in theta, which is the paper's lim. No InjOn, no Cauchy-surface field. trace_tendsto_atTop_of_complete (l.411) drops R'' and needs only 0 < R. hpos is implied by the strict lem_blunt_spear output (v + R'/2 < tauS z, BluntSpear.lean:1058), so the chain composes. Lean >= target. NON-VACUITY (the key check): the hypothesis set is SATISFIABLE. Instance (mathematical, no Lean term): N = the flat regular part {r>0} of E0 (Reg of the BTZE0 component; note it is not e0RegMFlat E0Y literally, since E0Y = M ⊕ BTZE0 is not connected, but Reg(BTZE0) ≅ R × C* via toPaper is connected and Hausdorff, a FlatSpacetime.{0} 2), W = paperInY '' {rad > 0} (open, contains bspearY 0 1), psi = the identification of regular points (an E0-morphism: locally inl ∘ g • btzPaperDev, the same chart flatE0_regChart/graphDev_eq_shift_sectorChartY express), v = 0, R = 1, R'' = 1/2, tauS z = 1/|z|, Sig = psi(paperInY {x | rad x > 0, x.1 = 1/rad x}). Binder by binder: hR 0<1; hc 1/|z| continuous on z≠0; hpos |z|/2 < 1/|z| iff |z|^2 < 2, true for |z| <= 1; hgraph: psi∘paperInY injective on rad>0 (toPaper is a homeomorphism), so psi(paperInY x) ∈ Sig iff x.1 = 1/|x.2|, for every x ∈ bspear 0 1 including the closed rim fcoord = 0 (nothing in the statement restricts to a closed strip, unlike SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDev g R)). Metric: btzPaperDev_pullback (Model.lean:1486) gives minkQ(dD(dtau,dr,dtheta)) = -2 dtau dr + dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2 in the strict convention (tau = x.1 of E0 = R × C, confirmed by graphDev = btzPaperDev ∘ graphMap and traceFun tauS (r,theta) = tauS(r e^{i theta})); on tau = 1/r, dtau = -dr/r^2, so the induced form is (1 + 2/r^2) dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2. Correct; it also matches the paper's own criterion of lem:surface_complete (i) (l.784: 1 - 2 d_r tau - (d_theta tau / r)^2 = 1 + 2/r^2 >= C^2/r^2 with C = sqrt 2). The development is a local diffeomorphism on r > 0 (Jacobian det -2r), so Sig is a smooth embedded surface with positive-definite induced metric; IsSpacelikeLipschitz (CauchyComplete.lean:526: point-local IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn, achronal in V plus local graph of slope c < 1 in an isometric frame) holds with V a small convex neighbourhood in the chart. Completeness: the length uses Lipschitz-in-charts paths with density sqrt(minkQ(deriv)) (CauchyComplete.lean:172, 314), which on paths of Sig equals the Riemannian density a.e.; with rho' = sqrt(1+2/r^2), rho' >= sqrt2/r near 0 and >= 1, so the distance is >= |Δrho|, Cauchy sequences stay in a compact annulus where the induced length is bi-Lipschitz to the coordinate metric, hence CompleteSpace. Continuity of toSubtype: the form dominates dr^2 + r^2 dtheta^2 = |dz|^2, so |Δz| <= induced distance and tau = 1/|z| follows; toSubtype is continuous. Conclusion 1/r -> +infinity holds, as it must. ROUTE: genuine. exists_traceSig equates the induced length of the image path with the pulled length through trace_chart_local and the strict Causal.Flat.pathLength_pulled_eq_of_local; pathLength_seg_unif bounds each straight piece; brokenLine/continuous_brokenLine make the curve; vertices Cauchy in InducedLengthSpace, whole broken line converges by edist_le_pathLength, then in N by htop, contradicting GX.E0AxisNoLimit.flat_curve_noLimit (l.580). hcomp of trace_tendsto_atTop is never assumed. FINDING (REPORT): « Since Sigma_0 is complete, by Lemma lem:surface_complete lim tau_0 = +infinity » is correctly classified as a missing step, not an error: lem:surface_complete (ii) (l.781-790) needs the graph over D_R^* itself to be complete; Sigma_0 ∩ S is not complete merely as a piece of a complete Sigma_0 unless one knows a finite-length curve with r -> 0 has no limit in M_0, which is exactly flat_curve_noLimit. The conclusion of the paper is true and the Lean supplies the step.

findings.what: The second occurrence of « by Lemma lem:surface_complete lim tau_0 = +infinity » is at BTZ_1.tex l.1604 of papers/btz/legacy/labeled/BTZ_1.tex, not l.1603 (l.1603 is the paragraph defining the circles C, C', C'' and N). The finding itself is sound.
findings.fix: Write l.1601 (and again l.1604) when the finding is carried into the ledger row's paper_findings.

findings.what: The instance is checked by hand only (no Lean term), which kb/0011 permits; it is correct. For whoever builds the term later: the in-tree Causal.Flat.FlatSpacetime constructor for it is not e0RegMFlat E0Y (E0Y = Minkowski ⊕ BTZE0 is not connected, so ConnectedSpace fails); it must be Reg of the BTZE0 component, e.g. e0RegMFlat of the open inr-range of E0Y, or FlatSpacetime.of on Reg(BTZE0). The docstring's wording (« the flat regular part {r > 0} of E0 ») is already right; the T-btz-axis-nolimit audit's « N = e0RegMFlat E0Y » is the imprecise one.
findings.fix: None required here; optionally add « (Reg of the BTZE0 component, not e0RegMFlat E0Y) » to the instance paragraph.
